prompt_en: At midday under the harsh sun, a salt worker rakes salt with a long wooden rake across a salt field, white mounds of salt lined up in rows on the ground.
refined_prompt: At midday under the harsh sun, a salt worker rakes salt with a long wooden rake across a salt field, white mounds of salt lined up in rows on the ground. In the heart of summer in Vietnam, at midday when the sun is at its peak, a salt worker meticulously rakes salt across a vast salt field, stretching as far as several football fields. Rows of white salt mounds, neatly arranged and glistening under the intense sunlight, cover the landscape. The worker uses a long wooden rake, known as a "cào muối gỗ," to carefully spread the salt across the field, each movement deliberate, scraping and spreading the salt to ensure it is evenly distributed and of the highest quality. The rhythmic sound of the rake scraping against the salt is accompanied by the shimmering light reflecting off the salt crystals, while the smell of salt water fills the air. Each salt mound, roughly the size of a large dining table, is precisely spaced to ensure optimal exposure to the sun and wind for the drying process. This practice, deeply rooted in the cultural fabric of Vietnam, has been celebrated in folklore and festivals for generations.
